column1: How does Zermelo (1908) avoid Russell's paradox?
column2: Sets are built only as subsets of sets that already exist, by listed axioms. With later additions and the axiom of choice this is ZFC.

column1: Gödel's first incompleteness theorem (1931), in plain words?
column2: Any consistent formal system with machine-listable axioms that does basic arithmetic has a statement it can neither prove nor disprove.

column1: Gödel's second incompleteness theorem, in plain words?
column2: Such a system cannot prove its own consistency, unless it is inconsistent.

column1: Why is the halting problem undecidable?
column2: If halts(P, x) existed, build trouble(P): loop if halts(P, P), else stop. trouble(trouble) halts exactly when it does not: contradiction.

column1: Who first reconstructs the Enigma rotor wiring, and when?
column2: Marian Rejewski of the Polish Cipher Bureau, December 1932, using permutation theory.

column1: What is the key idea of the 1945 EDVAC report?
column2: The stored program: memory holds both instructions and data, and the CPU fetches and executes them.

column1: What does the simplex method (Dantzig, 1947) solve?
column2: Linear programming: maximize or minimize a linear goal under linear limits, by walking from corner to better corner.
